tagline: Pioneering wireless technologies and chipsets for the connected intelligent edge
hero_kpi_rationale: The 16% growth in the QCT segment (equipment) highlights Qualcomm's strategic positioning in chips for premium smartphones, IoT, and automotive. This segment represents 85% of total revenue and drives the transition toward edge AI and connected intelligent devices, a major structural lever for the company.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue that remains after paying direct production costs.
kpis.description: Gross margin declines to 55% in 2025 from 56% in 2024, primarily due to a lower share of licensing revenues (QTL), which carry higher margins.
kpis.signal: Margin declining despite sales growth, linked to reduced contribution from the highly profitable licensing segment.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Profit generated before taxes and interest, expressed as a percentage of total revenue.
kpis.description: Calculated from operating income (revenue minus costs minus R&D), operating margin stands at approximately 18.5% in 2025. This estimate requires validation as the $5.7 B tax charge impacts net income but not operating income directly.
kpis.signal: Significant decline in operating margin in 2025, impacted by an exceptional tax charge that affected net income but not operating income directly.

kpis.name: R&D Spending (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenues reinvested in research and development of new technologies.
kpis.description: R&D expenses reach $9.0 B in 2025, or 20% of revenue, up in absolute value (+$149 M) but down as a percentage from 23% in 2024, due to faster revenue growth (+14%).
kpis.signal: High R&D spending, typical for a fabless semiconductor leader, despite relative decline due to faster revenue growth.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned by the company over a year.
kpis.description: Total revenue reaches $44.3 B in 2025, up 14% from $39.0 B in 2024, driven by growth in the QCT (equipment and services) segment, which increases by 16%.
kpis.signal: Significant revenue rebound in 2025, driven by chip sales for smartphones, IoT, and automotive.

kpis.name: Equipment Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the sale of chips and integrated technologies in devices.
kpis.description: The QCT (Qualcomm CDMA Technologies) segment generates $37.9 B in revenue in 2025, up 16% (+$5.1 B) year-on-year, supported by stronger demand in handsets, IoT, and automotive.
kpis.signal: Robust growth in core business, with accelerating launches of premium smartphones, IoT, and automotive applications.

kpis.name: Licensing Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from royalties collected for the use of patented technology.
kpis.description: The QTL (Qualcomm Technology Licensing) segment reports revenues of $6.4 B in 2025, up $244 M (+4%) from $6.2 B in 2024, including $143 M from a litigation settlement in Q2.
kpis.signal: Stable licensing revenues despite disputes, supported by a one-time $143 M settlement in Q2 2025.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Final profit after all expenses, taxes, and charges.
kpis.description: Net income drops to $5.5 B in 2025 from $10.1 B in 2024, due to an exceptional tax charge of $5.7 B related to the write-down of deferred tax assets following the adoption of the OBBB reform on July 4, 2025.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in net income in 2025 despite sales growth, due to a $5.7 B exceptional tax charge.

kpis.name: Exceptional Tax Charge
kpis.explanation: One-time loss related to a tax reform impacting future assets.
kpis.description: In Q4 2025, QCOM records a $5.7 B charge to establish a valuation allowance against federal deferred tax assets following the adoption of the OBBB (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) on July 4, 2025, which introduces the CAMT starting in 2026.
kpis.signal: Major impact of a U.S. tax reform (OBBB) on 2025 profitability, with the introduction of CAMT from 2026.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale. Indicateur clé pour les investisseurs orientés revenus.
kpis.description: 5-year history of declared dividends per share (2021-2025).

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel du cash redistribué aux actionnaires : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury stock).
kpis.description: For 2025: cumulative dividends + share buybacks in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée en dividendes. Au-dessus de 80 % indique un dividende potentiellement non-soutenable.
kpis.description: Dividends / net income for 2025 (based on net income attributable to shareholders).

risks.title: Loss in value of deferred tax assets
risks.score_rationale: The risk is stated to result in a $5.7 billion charge in 2025 due to CAMT, a major regulatory change. The language is definitive ("no longer expect to realize substantially all"). The Capital category is heavily weighted here. This risk is new and existential for the tax structure.

risks.title: Uncertain accounting estimates
risks.score_rationale: The risk factor is repeated across multiple line items (revenue, inventory, taxes, assets). Although variances were marginal in 2024-2025, the document emphasizes that differences could be "material." Central placement in the 10-K and cautious language.

risks.title: Risks related to non-public investments
risks.score_rationale: Portfolio of $1.4 B across 150 companies, often early-stage. The text mentions risks of illiquidity, depreciation, and stock market exposure. While no significant losses have been recorded, the risk is structural and recurring.

risks.title: Legal and regulatory disputes
risks.score_rationale: The document states potential losses could exceed provisions, and outcomes are "inherently uncertain." Explicit mention of exposure to material losses. Recurring risk with high intensity.

risks.title: Foreign exchange rate fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: Exposure of $2.2 B in tax receivables in Korea: a 10% rate change would cost $223 M. The risk is quantified and active, but partially hedged. Mentioned in market risks.

risks.title: Inventory depreciation
risks.score_rationale: The risk relates to customer demand and macroeconomic conditions. Although recent impact is <1%, the text highlights a margin risk if demand collapses. Industrial category, moderate intensity.

ai_positioning.summary: The company QCOM does not explicitly mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report.
